findings.F1: The test's result points the way the idea predicts but stays far short of the bar: slope t 0.87 (500 grid cases on 208 days), unusual move in the short direction +0.32 % (t 0.75, 530 days), strength 0.030 of a usual 11.68 % move. The coins' normal drift of −0.69 % against the short turns the total move to −0.38 %. The test already used all four folds and all 19 coins on daily bars, so no more data is available.
findings.F2: In folds B and C the effect is clearer over 10 days than over the plan's 5. Among the signalled bars, the day-clustered slope t is 2.20 at 10 days (92 cases, 55 days), against 1.54 at 5 days and 1.65 at 3 days. The mean unusual move in the short direction is 2.7 % at 10 days, against 2.0 % at 5.

findings.F4: The 5-day result depends on which 5-day grid is used. On grid offset 0 the short unusual move is 2.0 % (t 2.34). On offsets 1 to 4 it is only 0.8 % to 1.1 % (t 0.8 to 1.1), with slope t of −0.10, 1.23, 1.65 and −0.95. At 5 days the grading is mostly noise.

findings.F6: Inside the choppy calm profile, the bars with the largest 5-day falls are followed by lower returns than the rest. The lowest quintile of past 5-day returns (mean −7.7 %) is followed by a −3.8 % excess 5-day return (t −2.86, 47 cases) and −6.0 % over 10 days. The two rising quintiles are followed by +1.0 % and +1.3 %, and bars with no signal by +0.6 %.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, calm market, a coin whose 5-day return is more negative, measured against its 30-day daily swing, falls further over the next 10 days. The larger the swing-scaled 5-day fall, the larger the further fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorting a coin after a fall that is large for its quiet swing should expect the further fall to build over about ten days, not five, and should size it by the size of the fall.
ideas.name: choppy calm falls, ten days
